page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated Intel x86_64 processor. The instance features 1 physical CPU core with 2 hyperthreads (2 vCPUs) paired with 16 GB of System RAM, providing an 8 GB per vCPU memory ratio. The CPU features 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. Advanced instruction set support includes Intel AMX (tile and int8) and AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16), alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance contains no attached local NVMe storage and includes zero bundled public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark testing, the n4-highmem-2 instance demonstrates moderate single-core processing capabilities alongside constrained multi-core and memory throughput performance. Single-thread workloads achieve average results, recorded at a Geekbench single-core score of 1640.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1554.59. However, multi-core scaling is limited by the two-thread capacity, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 2036.0 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 1600.79. Memory bandwidth tests show lower overall throughput, with uncached 256 MB sequential reads measuring 15.05 GB/sec and writes at 9.22 GB/sec.

The server offers entry-level compute capacity with elevated RAM density, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-sensitive services that do not demand heavy parallel processing. It exhibits low throughput in database operations (931.96 ops in PassMark) and Redis SET operations (2.24 million ops/sec). Workload suitabilities include lightweight in-memory caching, microservices, small background workers, or light text-processing tasks requiring modest CPU overhead but higher memory headroom.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 2 vCPUs powered by a single physical Intel x86_64 core with hyperthreading and 16 GB of RAM, delivering an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU allocation. Hardware features include 260 MB of L3 cache, hardware cryptography engines, and advanced vector acceleration via Intel AMX and AVX-512. The instance contains no local NVMe storage and zero GPUs. Benchmark evaluation indicates average single-core capabilities, recorded with a 1640.0 Geekbench single-core score and 26.16 GB/sec single-threaded gzip throughput. Multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are bounded by the low core count, resulting in 15.05 GB/sec uncached memory read bandwidth. Qualitatively, n4-highmem-2 delivers efficient resource allocation for memory-heavy workloads with limited parallel CPU needs, such as small in-memory caches, lightweight microservices, and basic background text processing tasks.
